coord_note: dx = px_in_cell/288 - 0.5, dy = px_in_cell/288 - 0.5. The cell is drawn filling -size*ar/2..+size*ar/2 by -size/2..+size/2.

WARNING_ar_differs_between_poses.why_it_matters: drawOutfit computes cx = anchor.dx * size * ar. Because ar is 1.3061 for idle but 1.0 for the moving sheet, the SAME dx produces a different pixel offset in each pose. A moving-pose dx must be read off this file, never copied from the idle file. To convert an idle dx to the equivalent pixel offset in the moving pose: dx_moving = dx_idle * 1.3061.

head_moves_between_poses.comment: The head sits ~0.115 of sprite height LOWER (less negative dy) in the moving sheet than in idle. This is the drift the user reported: an idle-tuned dy of -0.36 lands well above the moving head.

loop_variation.comment: dx is very stable across the loop (spread 0.019 of sprite width) so one moving dx is safe. dy wobbles more (spread 0.063) as the dragon flaps; the mean is the best single value and worst case is about +/-0.03 off.

char_airborne.comment: Airborne is a steep nose-down dive: the head is LOW (dy +0.273, i.e. below centre) and far forward, while the topmost point of the silhouette is the raised tail/wing at dy -0.486. An idle- or moving-tuned anchor will be badly wrong here - airborne needs its own values, and its head_center dy differs from idle by 0.42 of sprite height.

confidence: head_bbox / head_center / head_top use the same heuristic as the idle file (rightmost 28% of the red region), so they still include some upper body. snout_tip, topmost, back_top and all bboxes are exact. No eye landmark is attempted here - the idle file's eye_center was unreliable and the same method would be no better on a 288px cell.
